summary: The legal input length is capped at 100, and the existing scaling benchmark did not distinguish a correct repeated-slicing quadratic implementation. A matching worst-case linear lower bound directly certifies the candidate's optimality.

optimality.argument: For an n-digit input containing only nines, an unchecked position could instead contain a smaller digit and absorb the carry, changing the result. Any correct algorithm must therefore inspect Omega(n) digits in the worst case. The candidate moves one cursor left and visits each digit at most once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: On an all-nine input, every digit must be ruled out as the first position from the right that can absorb the carry; changing any unread digit below nine changes the required output.
The candidate's cursor decreases monotonically, and each visited digit is either incremented once before returning or changed from nine to zero once.
The source-fidelity-verified examples include both immediate carry absorption and carry overflow; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
